neighbours.label: pieces of British (especially northern English) upland place names: fells, pikes, moors, dales and lakes (Skiddaw, Helvellyn, North York Moors)
fire: On the second day we climbed Blencathra by the Sharp Edge route.
The reservoir at Haweswater drowned the old village of Mardale.
From the top of Whernside you can see Ingleborough to the south.
We followed the beck down into Borrowdale before the rain came.
The farm sits at the head of Wensleydale near Hawes.
Mist covered Great Gable as we left Wasdale Head.
Walkers crossing Kinder Scout should carry a compass.
The path drops from Scafell Pike towards Eskdale.
quiet: On the second day we climbed Mount Whitney by the main trail.
The reservoir at Hetch Hetchy drowned a beautiful valley.
From the top of Mount Hood you can see Mount Jefferson to the south.
We followed the creek down into the canyon before the rain came.
The farm sits at the head of the valley near the old church.
Mist covered the Matterhorn as we left Zermatt.
Walkers crossing the Rocky Mountains should carry a compass.
The path drops from Mont Blanc towards Chamonix.

notes: Card: Hellgill Wold, Sheffield Pike, Lake District, Great Dun Fell, St Bees Head, Blackwater of Dee. The opposite pole fires on the preposition before English counties.
